title: Single-step SU(3) Hahn Echo in a Qutrit Atom Interferometer
authors: Chirantan Mitra, Lucas Gabardos, François Impens, David Guéry-Odelin, David Wilkowski, Chang Chi Kwong
abstract: The Hahn echo is a well-known dynamical decoupling method that refocuses the dephasing due to energy inhomogeneities of a spin-1/2 ensemble and is widely used to extend phase coherence in quantum computers and sensors. Extensions of such techniques beyond the spin-1/2 have been reported, but have mainly used SU(2) gates, limiting their scalability. Here, we generalize the Hahn echo to qutrits using single-step SU(3) gates and extend the coherence time by more than an order of magnitude. The gates are generated through optimal control theory and implemented in an ultracold atomic ensemble in free fall. A quantum process tomography procedure benchmarks the gates and yields fidelities of ~ 93%, limited mainly by state preparation and measurement errors. Due to the geometry of the laser beams, the generalized Hahn echo also realizes a three-path Mach-Zehnder atomic interferometer with two independent interferometric phase differences. Our results therefore establish SU(3) control for dynamical decoupling of qutrits and multi-path atom interferometers, with the latter opening the possibility for vector force measurements and interferometric tests of the validity of Born's rule.
summary: This research generalizes the Hahn echo dynamical decoupling method to qutrits using single-step SU(3) gates implemented in ultracold strontium atoms. By employing optimal control theory, the authors significantly extend the coherence time and demonstrate the capability to build multi-path atomic interferometers. This establishes a robust platform for high-dimensional quantum sensing and computation.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of extending dynamical decoupling techniques, like the Hahn echo, from qubits (spin-1/2) to qutrits ($d=3$) to preserve quantum coherence in multi-level atomic systems.
main_result: They successfully generalized the Hahn echo using single-step SU(3) gates, extending the coherence time by over an order of magnitude and realizing a three-path Mach-Zehnder interferometer.
method: The gates were generated using optimal control theory (OCT) and implemented experimentally in an ultracold atomic ensemble in free fall, with performance benchmarked via quantum process tomography (QPT).
model_or_system: The physical system is an ultracold ensemble of Strontium-87 ($^{87}	ext{Sr}$) atoms, where the qutrit is encoded in three Zeeman ground states ($|0angle, |1angle, |2angle$). The dynamics are controlled using a tripod scheme involving internal atomic transitions.
key_observables: Dephasing time ($T_2$), interference fringe amplitudes, and gate fidelities ($\sim 93\%$).
important_parameters: Coherence time extension ($>10	imes$), gate fidelities, and the ability to measure two independent interferometric phase differences.
main_assumptions: The primary source of infidelity is attributed to State Preparation and Measurement (SPAM) errors, rather than the gate operations themselves.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows the decay of interference amplitudes for Ramsey vs. Hahn echo sequences. Figure 2 compares Ramsey and Hahn echo measurements, demonstrating the coherence improvement.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the need for SU(3) generalization, detailing the OCT-based gate implementation, measuring the resulting coherence time improvement via echo sequences, and finally demonstrating the realization of a multi-path interferometer.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it pushes the boundaries of quantum control into higher-dimensional Hilbert spaces (qudits) using state-of-the-art atomic platforms, directly impacting quantum sensing and computation.
